clue.text: Successful, exciting period for short scientific expedition

definitions.meaning: a time of great opportunity and enjoyment, as when one 'has a ___'
an outing for study in the open, such as a school geography or natural history trip

explanation.surface: A scientist reflects that a brief research trip turned out thrilling and productive.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase has both senses: a day of outdoor study and, figuratively, any time of gleeful opportunity.

clue.text: Mathematician takes a prolonged rest

parts.note: Pierre de Fermat was a French mathematician

explanation.surface: A mathematician takes a long break.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a fermata is a pause sign, holding a note or rest longer than written.

clue.text: European project that's unlikely to get off the ground

definitions.meaning: European Monetary Union, the scheme for a single currency

definitions.text: that's unlikely to get off the ground
definitions.meaning: a large Australian bird that cannot fly

explanation.surface: A Europe-wide plan seems doomed never to take off.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters are the abbreviation for European Monetary Union and the name of a flightless bird.

clue.text: Primitive blower is good —- I dried out

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker confesses that after drying out they are now well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GOOD I DRIED; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The didgeridoo is an ancient Aboriginal wind instrument, a primitive thing to blow.

clue.text: Latin is used for a particular reason

definitions.text: Latin is used for a particular reason

parts.words: Latin is used for a particular reason
parts.note: describes a Latin tag meaning 'for this purpose'

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'for this', applied to something arranged for one specific purpose.

clue.text: Lay into piece of machinery, having fit of pique

parts.note: a car is a machine on wheels
a pet is a sulky bout of bad temper, as in 'in a pet'

explanation.surface: Someone, in a temper, attacks a machine on the factory floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay into' looks physical, but here it means to scold severely.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to reprimand them sharply, summoning them as if onto the boss's rug.

clue.text: A princess in operetta, eponymous heroine

parts.note: Princess Ida is the title of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera

explanation.surface: A royal in a light opera is also the one it is named after.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan are the Victorian authors of English comic operettas.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera is named after its heroine, an Ethiopian princess, so she is eponymous.

clue.text: One could chew the fat, taking in this clerical feature

definitions.text: One could chew the fat, taking in this clerical feature

parts.words: One could chew the fat, taking in this clerical feature
parts.note: 'chew the fat' suggests chatting with a vicar, but means eating the fatty tail of a roast bird, named jokingly after a cleric

explanation.definitionFit: The fatty rump of a cooked fowl is jokingly named after a clergyman's facial feature.

clue.text: Little chap one's left a bit drunker

indicators.note: one has left, so that letter goes from the word

parts.note: tiddly means slightly drunk, so tiddlier is a bit drunker
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's means 'has'

explanation.surface: A small man has had one more and is slightly tipsier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddler is British slang for a small child or tiny fish, a little one.

clue.text: Capturing knight, abandon a popular medieval exercise

indicators.note: the word for abandon holds the knight inside it

parts.note: to quit is to abandon
N is the chess abbreviation for knight
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A medieval pastime involved seizing a knight and running away.
explanation.definitionFit: The quintain was a post or target that knights tilted at in medieval jousting practice.

clue.text: Having a hunch delivery task needs to be taken on

parts.note: a round is a regular delivery route, such as a milk or paper round
to have shouldered a burden is to have taken it on

explanation.surface: A delivery worker has a feeling that an extra job must be accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunch' suggests an intuition; it is a hunched back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with stooping, forward-curved shoulders has a hunch in the physical sense.

clue.text: One growing old left in a decline

indicators.note: the letters for old and left are placed inside the word for a decline

parts.note: a descent is a downward slope or decline

explanation.surface: An elderly person, left behind, is in a downward spiral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One growing old' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'growing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person still growing up towards adulthood.

clue.text: One may knock work left to one

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
port is the left side of a ship
unity is oneness, the number one

explanation.surface: Someone may criticise a job that was left to just one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock' suggests criticism; the saying is that this chance knocks only once.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says this chance only knocks once, so it is one that may knock.

clue.text: Ring's cost

definitions.meaning: to sound a bell slowly, as for a funeral
a charge paid, as for using a road or bridge

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the slow sounding of a bell and a fee paid for passage.

clue.text: Defendant receives cat, as usual

indicators.note: the defendant takes the cat inside

parts.note: the accused is the defendant in a trial
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: As usual, the person on trial is given a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Accustomed means customary or habitual, as in 'in her accustomed seat'.

clue.text: Asked for a couple of pages and made up a story

parts.note: PP is the abbreviation for pages, plural
to have lied is to have told an untruth

explanation.surface: Someone requested two pages and then invented a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: To have applied for something, such as a job, is to have formally requested it.

clue.text: Tedious condition, still under canvas here

definitions.meaning: a state of gloom, stagnation or inactivity
an ocean belt of calm near the equator where sailing ships lie becalmed

explanation.surface: Camping is still boring in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under canvas' suggests camping; here it means under sail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a dull, stagnant mood and the calm equatorial waters that becalm sailing ships.

clue.text: One charging a small volume to patron

parts.note: CC, cubic centimetre, is a small unit of volume
a patron of a service is one who uses it, a user

explanation.surface: A small book is being billed to a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charging' suggests billing; it is bringing a charge against someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser is one who charges another with wrongdoing.

clue.text: Flier at present left on counter

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece set on another comes after it, so the counter word goes first

parts.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
now means at present

explanation.surface: Someone currently on a flight has been left at a counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the other pieces after BAR in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This pale, ghostly bird is one kind of flier, a species of owl.

clue.text: Thrive? In Ulysses' family, sons not getting on

indicators.note: the shortened sons go inside the family name

parts.note: Leopold Bloom is the hero of Joyce's novel Ulysses

indicators.note: the word on is taken away from sons

explanation.surface: Can Ulysses' household prosper when the boys are not getting on?
explanation.walkthrough: 'not getting on' removes ON from SONS to leave SS.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to flourish or thrive, like a plant in flower.

clue.text: A number of Poles seizing new currency put in cells

indicators.note: the two poles grip the other letters between them

parts.note: more than one pole: N and S, the north and south poles
the euro is the currency of much of Europe

explanation.surface: Polish people grabbing new money end up locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' reads as people from Poland but gives the compass points; 'put in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurons are nerve cells, the units of the nervous system.

clue.text: Patron abandons all his love for English poet

indicators.note: every O in the patron's word, love being nil in tennis, is given up
each O is swapped for E, the abbreviation for English

parts.note: a sponsor is a patron

explanation.surface: A benefactor gives up all affection for an English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Os in SPONSOR (love is O, nil in tennis) become E for English, giving SPENSER.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan English poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Ancient river made circle to cross America

parts.note: O is a circle in shape
X is a cross in shape
US, the United States, stands for America

explanation.surface: An old river looped round so as to cut across America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'made circle' and 'cross' look like actions; they are the shapes O and X.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxus is the classical name of the Amu Darya river in Central Asia.

clue.text: Periodical supplement to work of police?

definitions.meaning: a regular publication; here a British satirical magazine of that name
a hired detective works alongside the official force

explanation.surface: A magazine supplement covers the work of the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names Britain's fortnightly satirical magazine and also a private detective.

clue.text: One of the selectors had seen bad over around start of test

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the first letter of test
the word over has gone bad, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A cricket selector watched a poor over at the start of a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had seen bad' makes VOER from OVER, which goes around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter is one who selects, choosing candidates at an election.

clue.text: Star, very mature, given lift

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting the word means reading it upwards

parts.note: to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A star, very mature, gets a facelift.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: The curse of piracy

parts.note: reads as the scourge of piracy, but means the oath that stage pirates exclaim

explanation.definitionFit: This is the stock exclamation of fictional sailors and pirates, an oath of surprise.

clue.text: Amphibian, though adroit, died out

indicators.note: the letter for died is taken out of the word

parts.note: deft means adroit or skilful

explanation.surface: An amphibian, though nimble, perished.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, a small amphibian.

clue.text: Cry of distress when bank shuts its doors

definitions.meaning: the international radio call for help
the early-May public holiday in Britain, a bank holiday

explanation.surface: Panic breaks out when a bank closes for good.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bank failing; British bank holidays close banks for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the radio distress signal and the first of May, a UK bank holiday.

clue.text: Ruthless type violently parted with gold

indicators.note: the letters of parted are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A brutal person was forcibly separated from their gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A predator is a person who ruthlessly exploits others, like a hunting animal.
